newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO eased on overnight crude plunge.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO eased on overnight crude plunge.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday eased on a overnight crude losses, traders said.
Late on Thursday 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil was sold by an oil major to a local trader at $119 per tonne for January 7-11 lifting fob Singapore.
Crude oil prices in Asia tumbled by over $1.00 a barrel late Wednesday. While it has rebounded, market sentiment remained depressed, traders said.
January swaps last traded at $118 per tonne, under Wednesday's indications of $120.25/$121 per tonne.
But some traders remained bullish, citing support from a higher freight costs that have capped Middle East supplies to the east.
Traders said Gulf-to-Singapore freight rates have risen by $2.00 per tonne since last week.
They said Chinese enquries have subsided as buyers were sitting at the sidelines waiting for a clearer indication from potential sellers.
They said South Korean export supplies in January were expected to be around December volumes.
